title: Separate proof debt from rules no guard can settle, and bind claims to heads
body:
PHASE 3. Both artifacts exist to stop a number meaning less than it looks like.

## Proof obligations

The doctor's "unguarded external-effect directives" mixed two things. A prohibition on an external effect can be settled by removing the protection and watching a test go red. A **permission** cannot be settled that way by anyone — granting latitude has no failure state to catch. Counting them together produced a review queue that read as a defect list, and reading all 22 by hand was the only way to tell which was which.

Now it is computed, over 262 directives:

| obligation kind | total | discharged | outstanding |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NOT_DISCHARGEABLE_BY_CODE` | 43 | — | **n/a, by nature** |
| `INTERNAL_TEST` | 177 | 143 | 34 |
| `MUTATION_GUARD` | 31 | 20 | 11 |
| `EXECUTABLE_CHECK` | 11 | 8 | 3 |

**The number worth acting on is 14** — rules code could settle that it has not. Smaller and truer than "19 unguarded", and the first one that is actually a work queue.

The kinds are ordered most-demanding-first, because an external-effect prohibition *also* matches the weaker `INTERNAL_TEST` rule, and filing it there would let a test that merely mentions the subject discharge it. A mention is not enforcement — that distinction is what the whole constitution effort turns on, and it is guarded.

## Claim-evidence registry

This repository asserts things about itself. Each was true of some tree at some moment, and nothing checked whether that moment is this one. It has already gone wrong twice here: a constitution artifact merged claiming 464 anchors against a tree holding 469, and a readiness artifact describing a commit whose source had since changed.

Running it immediately flagged four stale claims from artifacts generated before the last squash merge. Regenerating cleared them — the check working, not a coincidence.

**One finding from building it:** the canonical-V9 claim originally cited the blocker document, which records one investigation and goes stale by design. It now cites the gap ledger, which re-runs the materializer at whatever head it reports. A claim should point at the thing that re-measures it.

## A flaw my own test caught

Comparing a claim's recorded head against current HEAD is **unsatisfiable** — committing the artifact changes HEAD, so a registry generated immediately before a commit is stale the moment it lands. Every commit would produce a red gate, and a staleness signal that fires on everything trains a reader to ignore the word.

Staleness is now about **source**, the question `canon-freshness` already asks: has any source the claim depends on changed since it was measured? A stale claim names the files that falsified it. An unreadable commit range is handled separately and is *worse* than stale — a recorded head that cannot be found is a claim whose basis was rewritten, and reporting that as "no changes" would be the exact inversion.

## The absent artifacts, classified

Seventeen absent was not actionable; the reason each is absent is:

| reason | count |
|---|---|
| `COMPUTABLE_NOW` | 6 |
| `NEEDS_EXTERNAL_REALITY` | 5 |
| `NEEDS_REPEATED_OBSERVATION` | 4 |
| `NEEDS_A_RUNTIME_THAT_DOES_NOT_EXIST` | 1 |
| `NEEDS_ELAPSED_TIME` | 1 |

Writing `quadrillion-runtime-status.json` for a lattice runtime that does not exist would be precisely the confusion the doctrine names — a spec mistaken for an implemented search engine, in file form. An absence with no reason is now reported as a defect in the index, which is how the last unclassified one was caught.

## Also caught by existing gates

The anchor-integrity test found `V7CLAIM-01` pointing at a line the freshness fix had replaced — *"a mutation whose anchor is gone verifies nothing."* Repaired and re-killed.

## Verification at `b60e0a89`

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `test:deterministic` | 7717 tests, 7663 pass, **0 fail**, 54 skipped |
| `test:mutation-war:full` | **496 mutations, 496 killed, 0 not killed** |
| `check:syntax` | 2184 files parse |
| anchor integrity + verdict honesty | 18/18 pass |
| canon + constitution freshness | pass |

22 new tests. 12 new guards across this PR's two commits, each killed individually and in the full run.

No external effects. No authority widened. `softwareOpen` is 2 and `sourceSideComplete` is **false** — this PR does not claim the program is finished, and the ledger would refuse to say so.

title: Turn a real health probe into evidence, and stop the ledger reading complete
body:
Two ends existed and nothing joined them. `waitForUberLitHealth` probes a running service and returns a status; the Ubercel doctor reads contract-bound `AUTHENTICATED_HEALTH` signals and reports SERVING or NOT_SERVING from them. Between the two there was nothing.

So a **real probe** — `/api/health` returning 200 against the live Render deployment, recorded in `CURRENT_HANDOFF_2026-09-17_LEADGEN_OFFERS_DEPLOYED.md` — sat in a document as a sentence while the doctor reported `UNKNOWN__ONLY_PROVIDER_BADGES`. Prose is not a signal.

## What the doctor says now

```
state: UNKNOWN__EVIDENCE_STALE
```

That probe is recorded with its actual provenance: observed at `2026-09-17T16:46:59.098Z` by the deployment session that landed `9df093b2`, **not by this one**. So it ages out, correctly.

That is the honest answer and the whole point of the distinction: *we knew the service was healthy at 16:46, and we do not know it now.* "We have no way to know" and "we knew, and the knowledge expired" are different problems, and only the second is waiting on time.

## What the bridge refuses

As important as what it does:

| refusal | why |
|---|---|
| never probes | running it cannot manufacture the evidence it records — a test replaces global `fetch` with a throw to hold that |
| a 200 from an undeclared URL binds to nothing | a 200 from somewhere else is a 200 from somewhere else |
| the right URL with the wrong status does not bind | `probe-status-is-not-the-declared-expected-status` |
| an unbound success is never `serving: true` | it would smuggle a SERVING verdict past the doctor |
| no observer → refused | a probe with no observer cannot later be told apart from one this repository invented |
| no readable time → refused | it could never be aged, so it could never be known stale |

An unbound probe is still **recorded**, not discarded — it is an observation somebody made, and throwing it away would lose the record of having looked.

## The part I had to undo

Closing V7G003's software half moved `softwareOpen` to 0 and the ledger to `sourceSideComplete: true`.

That was false. **Nineteen artifacts the contract names do not exist**, and a ledger with no row for them is not a ledger that found nothing. `V7G009` now counts them from the artifact index — which reads `statSync`, not intent, so an empty file cannot close it.

```
softwareOpen 1, externalOpen 5, unmeasured 0
sourceSideComplete: false
```

Which is the true state.

## The five external gaps

Each names what would unblock it, because the ledger refuses an external claim that doesn't:

| gap | class | unblocked by |
|---|---|---|
| `V7G001` canonical V9 | EXTERNAL_SOURCE_ARTIFACT | founder supplies the V7 or V9 file |
| `V7G002` operative canon unranked | FOUNDER_ONLY | founder ranks the canon in the precedence file |
| `V7G003` deployment | EXTERNAL_BLOCKED | any authorized caller records a fresh contract-bound probe |
| `V7G006` no cleared payment | EXTERNAL_BLOCKED | one provider-witnessed payment reaches durable storage |
| `V7G007` no configured provider | EXTERNAL_BLOCKED | one provider configured, one routed call leaving a receipt |

title: V9 carrier repair, and the V7 gap ledger computed from source
body:
Executes `CLAUDE_START_V9.md`. Canonical V9 **could not be materialized**, and establishing precisely why is most of this PR.

## The carrier

`python3 scripts/materialize-inevitability-v9.py` reported `SEED_ENCODED_PART_MISMATCH:part-0001.xz.b64` and stopped. That reads as total corruption. It was not.

Fifteen of sixteen seed parts were each **exactly one byte short** — a stripped trailing newline. Restoring it makes every one of their encoded SHA-256 hashes match the manifest exactly, which is proof rather than inference. Fourteen are repaired here; part 7 had already been repaired in `8daf918a`, which is why it alone verified.

**Part 16 is different.** 6,500 bytes where the manifest requires 12,933 — short 4,823 binary bytes of LZMA-compressed V7 content. Six recovery mechanisms, all failed with certain outcomes:

| mechanism | result |
|---|---|
| sibling branch `-v2` | identical 6,500-byte truncation |
| sibling branch `-v3` | declares an 8-part schema-5.0.0 layout, commits **zero** parts |
| all 36,521 git objects scanned by size | **zero** blobs match V7's 1,916,551 bytes |
| Brotli carrier `-v1` | declares `partCount: 128`, holds 2 |
| large-blob survey | nothing resembling V7/V8/V9 |
| generator inspection | intact and SHA-verified, but forward-only and refuses any seed whose hash differs |

The truncated stream still decodes **96.3% of V7** before simply ending, mid-sentence at directive 1510. The remainder is absent, not damaged.

Wallbreaker receipt `wbr_c63017e3fd1a01caec01828a` selected external-source acquisition and ruled two candidates **ineligible by hard constraint**: brute-forcing the missing bytes (`no-fabricated-bytes`) and editing the manifest so the short carrier passes (`no-manifest-hash-weakening`). Those are the two shapes this failure invites, and both are refused in code.

The verifier is **unweakened** — `LOSSLESS_VERIFIED` still requires every hash. What changed is the failure path: all sixteen parts are checked before reporting, a part repairable without any source is separated from one that is not, and the report names the artifact and hash that would close it. A verifier that stops at the first symptom hides the shape of the damage, and the shape is the part a human can act on.

Blocker recorded at `artifacts/v9/canonical-v9-materialization-blocker.json`.

## A harness repair the above required

Mutation-war validated every mutant with `node --check`, so a mutation of **any** `.py` file reported `MUTANT_DID_NOT_PARSE` however well-formed it was. No Python in this repository could ever be guarded — including the one script standing between a partial carrier and a hash-locked artifact. The checker now follows the language. Verified not to regress JS mutants.

## PHASE 0 + PHASE 1

Canonical V9 is unavailable, so execution proceeds from the recoverable V7 ancestor and **every artifact says so in a field, not a footnote**: `executedFrom: PARTIAL_V7_ANCESTOR__EXPLICITLY_NOT_CANONICAL_V9`.

The gap ledger's contract is three sentences, all about the same failure: *a label never closes a gap, a stale artifact never closes a gap, a self-authored claim never closes an external gap.* So no gap carries a writable status — each owns a check that runs the materializer, a doctor, a ratchet, or git.

```
EXTERNAL_BLOCKED   EXTERNAL V7G001-CANONICAL-V9-NOT-MATERIALIZED
FOUNDER_ONLY       FOUNDER  V7G002-OPERATIVE-CANON-UNRANKED
OPEN               SOFTWARE V7G003-DEPLOYMENT-HAS-NO-CONTRACT-BOUND-HEALTH-EVIDENCE
CLOSED             SOFTWARE V7G004-UNGUARDED-EXTERNAL-EFFECT-DIRECTIVES
OPEN               SOFTWARE V7G005-VERIFIED-WORK-STRANDED-OFF-MAIN
EXTERNAL_BLOCKED   EXTERNAL V7G006-NO-EXTERNAL-ECONOMIC-EVIDENCE
EXTERNAL_BLOCKED   EXTERNAL V7G007-PROVIDER-EVALUATION-BLOCKED
CLOSED             SOFTWARE V7G008-EVERY-PRODUCTION-MODULE-GATED
softwareOpen 2, externalOpen 4, unmeasured 0
```

Three refusals fall out and each is guarded: a check that throws records `CHECK_FAILED` rather than collapsing into OPEN or CLOSED; a gap claiming an external blocker without naming what would unblock it falls back to OPEN (`EXTERNAL_BLOCKED, reason: pending` is exactly the forbidden label); and source-side completion requires zero *unmeasured* gaps as well as zero open ones, or a broken check becomes a way to finish.

## The artifact index

The contract names 29 artifacts and also says to reuse existing source where equivalent capability exists. Generating 29 files would produce mostly stubs and bury the few carrying real measurement. So each name resolves to `GENERATED` (2), `COVERED_BY_EXISTING_ARTIFACT` with what that cover actually holds (8), or `ABSENT` (19) — and **ABSENT stays counted**. Verified against the contract text: 29 declared, 29 mapped, none dropped.

## Two inherited red gates, closed

`src/leadgen-live-snapshot.mjs` arrived with the Apollo wiring and the production-coverage ratchet found it reachable with no gate. Verified red on main itself. The invariant that matters is that suppression records survive the trip from storage to handoff — if they stopped, suppressed people would enter a handoff with every check green, because an empty suppression list looks exactly like nobody having asked to be left alone. My first draft asserted a suppressed prospect appears marked blocked; it does not, and the real behaviour is stronger (excluded before becoming a row). Main had independently written a test for the same module covering the collections it added — kept **both**, since they cover different halves.

The second was the constitution freshness check from last session doing its job: the committed artifact said 477 anchors while the tree had 480.

| `test:deterministic` | 7695 tests, 7641 pass, **0 fail**, 54 skipped |
| `test:mutation-war:full` | **484 mutations, 484 killed, 0 not killed** |
| `check:syntax` | 2178 files parse |

title: Read deployment state through Ubercel instead of off a vendor's badge
body:
**Ubercel already existed, and I misreported it.**

`src/ubercel-deployment-control-plane.mjs` treats `VERCEL` as one of five replaceable adapter types (`OWNED_LINUX`, `GENERIC_DOCKER`, `VERCEL`, `ORACLE_CLOUD`, `OTHER_REPLACEABLE`), refuses any adapter that declares `deploymentAuthority`, and carries this law:

```js
laws: ['EXACT_SIGNED_RELEASE_ONLY', 'NO_PROVIDER_IS_THE_CONTROL_PLANE', ...]
```

I then read a red Vercel commit status and reported it as UberBond's deployment truth — in a PR comment and twice in a PR body.

## Why the law didn't stop it

It was enforced at **plan** time and nowhere at **read** time. Ubercel could compile a deployment plan and a failover plan; it could not be asked *what is true now*. There was no `ubercel:doctor`, no deployment-state reporter of any kind. So the only readable thing was a vendor badge, and that is what got read.

## The distinction this adds

A provider badge is a fact about the provider. It becomes a fact about UberBond only if UberBond serves from it — a question the badge cannot answer about itself. Only a probe bound to the health contract UberBond declared, or liveness from a runtime UberBond owns, describes UberBond.

| evidence class | establishes serving | establishes not-serving |
|---|---|---|
| `PROVIDER_BADGE` | ✗ | ✗ |
| `AUTHENTICATED_HEALTH` (contract-bound) | ✓ | ✓ |
| `OWNED_RUNTIME_LIVENESS` | ✓ | ✓ |

So a red badge alone reports `UNKNOWN__ONLY_PROVIDER_BADGES` rather than `NOT_SERVING` — a vendor build failing may be a surface we don't serve from. A green badge alone reports the same, which is the more dangerous error in the other direction and the one a passing build invites.

## `npm run ubercel:doctor`, against the signals as actually observed

```
ubercel deployment — uberbondd
  state: UNKNOWN__ONLY_PROVIDER_BADGES
  contract-bound authoritative signals: 0
  provider badges (each establishes nothing about UberBond):
    vercel [VERCEL] serving=false — github-commit-status:Vercel – uberbondd @ f19c52c7
    vercel-lite-private [VERCEL] serving=false — github-commit-status:Vercel – uberbondd-lite-private @ f19c52c7
  deploymentAuthority: NONE
```

That is the honest current state. **Nothing in this repository collects contract-bound health evidence yet**, and the doctor says so rather than letting an absence read as health.

The module is wired to a script rather than classified in `config/reachability-classification.json`, for the reason that config itself gives: *"a module reachable only from tests is not reachable."*

## On the other named layers

`uber-sovereign-stack.mjs` names 22 layers. Six have no uber-named module — and all six have substantial capability under their existing names:

| layer | existing modules | e.g. |
|---|---|---|
| `uberagents` | 21 | `agent-mesh-control-plane.mjs` |
| `ubereconomy` | 16 | `economic-metabolism.mjs` |
| `uberpay` | 14 | `billing-webhook-boundary.mjs` |
| `ubermodels` | 10 | `agent-model-router.mjs` |
| `uberdistribution` | 8 | `distribution-control-plane.mjs` |
| `ubervault` | 3 | `secret-patterns.mjs` |

**Naming gaps, not capability gaps.** Creating uber-named duplicates of these would be exactly the capability sprawl the canon prohibits ("Dedupe before adding code", "Never create a replacement UberBond app"), so they're left alone deliberately rather than by oversight. If you want the names unified, that's a rename with real reach and worth doing as its own change.

## Verification at `5c89108d`

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `test:deterministic` | 7654 tests, 7600 pass, **0 fail**, 54 skipped |
| `test:mutation-war:full` | **477 mutations, 477 killed, 0 not killed** |
| `check:syntax` | 2166 files parse |
| `reachability-ratchet` | 13/13 pass |

13 new tests. 5 new mutation guards, all killed: a badge establishing serving state, an authenticated probe counting while unbound from the declared contract, stale and future-dated evidence counting as current, an adapter promoting its own evidence, and one authenticated not-serving being outvoted by healthy ones.

## Boundary

No external effects. The doctor probes nothing and calls nothing — it reads evidence somebody else collected. `deploymentAuthority: NONE` on the report and on every admitted signal. This does not fix the Vercel build; it stops that build's badge from being mistaken for our deployment state, which is the part that was mine to fix.

title: Stop a stale constitution from describing a tree that has since changed
body:
`artifacts/constitution/directives.json` is what the Constitution Doctor prints its headline numbers from and what the review record is read against, and nothing verified it was current.

**It had already merged stale.** The artifact committed alongside the precedence work in #917 was generated *before* that same change added its test file and its five guards, so it recorded **464 mutation anchors against a tree holding 469** and named a test file that no longer existed. The doctor then reported those numbers in the present tense. Nothing failed, because nothing was looking.

A stale artifact here is not merely old. It answers *"which rules are enforced?"* about a tree that has moved on, confidently.

## Verified against the real failure, not a synthetic one

Run against the artifact exactly as it merged at `90dc631c`:

```
not ok 1 - the committed constitution artifact describes the current tree
    "field": "counts.mutationAnchorsAvailable",
    "committed": 464,
    "fresh": 469,
```

## Where the logic lives

In `src/constitution-artifact-freshness.mjs`, not inside the test — a comparison only a test performs is one no mutation can be pointed at. Headline counts are checked before the whole-document compare, because `469 !== 464` is a usable failure message and a diff of 262 directive objects is not.

## The reachability ratchet had the better idea

Its config is explicit:

> *"A module reachable only from tests is not reachable: the suite proves it behaves and proves nothing about whether anything can call it."*

Classifying the new module under `RESEARCH_ONLY` would have been a way of agreeing with the ratchet while ignoring it. Wiring it is also the more useful answer: the doctor regenerating a stale artifact in silence is *how a stale one gets committed* — the numbers come out right and nobody learns the file in git had been describing a different tree. It now reads what it is about to replace and reports the drift:

```
  the artifact just replaced was stale, and had been describing a different tree:
    counts.mutationAnchorsAvailable: committed 464, actual 472
```

A missing or unreadable previous artifact is not drift, so a first run is quiet.

## Verification at `73bdf315`

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `test:deterministic` | 7641 tests, 7587 pass, **0 fail**, 54 skipped |
| `test:mutation-war:full` | **472 mutations, 472 killed, 0 not killed** |
| `check:syntax` | 2163 files parse |
| `reachability-ratchet` | 13/13 pass |

3 new mutation guards, all killed: a differing artifact reported as current, the provenance exemption widened until any two artifacts compare equal, and the readable count comparison emptied into a bare document diff.

Still red, still red on `main` for the same pre-existing reason, still unreadable from this session (`403 Forbidden` on the project). Nothing in this diff reaches the deployed surface. Detail in [the standing-down comment on #916](https://github.com/mohammedwessam2007/uberbondd/pull/916#issuecomment-5707274431).

title: Make the constitution's precedence real, and say where it runs out
body:
The compiler's source list carried this comment:

> `/** Canon files, in precedence order. NORTH_STAR.md and the precedence file define that order. */`

False twice over. `docs/NORTH_STAR_PRECEDENCE.md` ranks ten files and **exactly one** of them is in that list. And every compiled directive carried `priority: 0`, so no order was applied even within it.

Fixing it turned up two facts worth having.

## The precedence law cannot settle any conflict between operative rules

| | count |
|---|---|
| files ranked by `docs/NORTH_STAR_PRECEDENCE.md` | 10 |
| operative sources compiled into directives | 9 |
| **in both** | **1** (`NORTH_STAR.md`) |
| conflict candidates detected | 9 |
| **resolvable by authored precedence** | **0** |

The files that actually bind an agent — `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `UBERBOND_CANON.md`, `AI_START_HERE.md` and the four `docs/*_CANON.md` — carry no relative rank anywhere in the repository. One of the nine conflicts is live: the Wallbreaker canon prohibits evading provider limits while CLAUDE.md permits automatic failover, and nothing says which governs.

**That is not mine to answer.** Ranking one canon file above another decides which rule wins in a real conflict, which is an amendment, and F003 says founder sovereignty rules are not autonomously modifiable. A compiler that picked an order would be legislating, and the order it picked would look authored to every later reader.

So:

- `precedenceFor()` returns `precedenceRank: null` with state `UNRANKED__NO_AUTHORED_PRECEDENCE`. The old `priority: 0` read as *highest* precedence — the opposite of the truth.
- `resolveByPrecedence()` refuses any pair with an unranked side and **names the source that needs a rank**.
- Both refusals are mutation-guarded (`CONSTPREC-01`, `CONSTPREC-02`).
- The question is recorded as **FD002** in `artifacts/constitution/open-founder-decisions.json` with three options — and with the note that ranking the operative canon in the precedence file resolves the graph **with no code change**, because the ranks are parsed from that file rather than transcribed here.

## The terminal layer's absence is now declared rather than merely true

The nine terminal North Star files hold **886 normative sentences**. Compiling them would take the constitution from 262 directives to ~1148, nearly all arriving as rules awaiting a guard.

`NORTH_STAR.md` states their status plainly — *"direction and search-space canon, not implementation proof"* — and a Directive Object asserts `REPOSITORY_TEST_OR_EXECUTABLE_CHECK`. Compiling them would make the opposite claim about all 886 and bury the 48 external-effect rules that bind behaviour today.

`TERMINAL_SOURCES` names them with that reason, and a test fails if a ranked file is ever neither compiled nor declared excluded — the silent-drop case the no-amputation law exists to prevent. This is a scope decision made visible, not an amputation: those files remain canon, are read at startup, and outrank every compiled directive on objective.

## Coverage rollup per source

"Which canon file is least enforced" is now answerable instead of one number spread across nine files:

| source | directives | guarded | ext-effect | ext guarded | gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `docs/AI_SKILL_PLUGIN_ASSIMILATION_CANON.md` | 51 | 12 | 8 | 4 | **4** |
| `UBERBOND_CANON.md` | 54 | 18 | 10 | 6 | **4** |
| `CLAUDE.md` | 28 | 13 | 9 | 6 | 3 |
| `docs/WALLBREAKER_CANON.md` | 19 | 8 | 6 | 4 | 2 |
| `docs/CAPABILITY_GENOME_CANON.md` | 33 | 10 | 5 | 3 | 2 |
| `AGENTS.md` | 40 | 12 | 6 | 4 | 2 |
| `NORTH_STAR.md` | 26 | 4 | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| `AI_START_HERE.md` | 7 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 1 |
| `docs/NORTH_STAR_PRECEDENCE.md` | 4 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 0 |

| gate | result |

| `test:deterministic` | 7639 tests, 7585 pass, **0 fail**, 54 skipped |
| `test:mutation-war:full` | **469 mutations, 469 killed, 0 not killed** |
| `check:syntax` | 2161 files parse |
| canon freshness | pass |

9 new tests. 5 new mutation guards, each confirmed killed individually and in the full run: an unranked source reporting as a rank, a conflict settled by inventing an order, two rules from one source ordered against each other, a duplicate entry hidden by taking the later rank, and the terminal layer going quietly absent.

title: Close the constitution review queue, and the four holes it found
body:
The Constitution Doctor reported 22 external-effect rules with no mutation guard behind them. That number was published as a review queue rather than a defect count, because a compound sentence, a keyword false positive and a real hole all land in it identically and only reading tells them apart. Five had been read. This reads the other seventeen.

**Four were real.** Three were invisible to reading alone — the code looks correct in each case — and only showed up by deleting the protection and watching every suite stay green.

### `src/wallbreaker.mjs` — a planner that could have acquired execution authority

WALLBREAKER_CANON: *"Every Wallbreaker result carries `businessEffectAuthority: NONE`."* The constant is set on ten return paths; three were asserted. Flipping the other seven to `FULL` changed nothing — `planWallbreakerCycle`'s success return among them.

```
line  51 -> SURVIVED      line 236 -> SURVIVED      line 301 -> SURVIVED
line  82 -> killed        line 257 -> SURVIVED      line 409 -> SURVIVED
line 165 -> SURVIVED      line 266 -> SURVIVED
line 206 -> SURVIVED      line 286 -> SURVIVED
```

All ten are now exercised; `WALLAUTH-01..03` ratchet the three that most resemble a real one.

### `src/egress-health-pool.mjs` — an assertion that passed for the wrong reason

This is where *"do not bypass CAPTCHA/platform controls"* becomes executable. The existing test asserted `ok === false` while supplying **no routes**, so it was satisfied by "no eligible route" and stayed green with the policy refusal deleted:

```
drop prohibited-purpose check -> SURVIVED
drop spoofing check           -> killed     (this one supplied a route, so it had teeth)
drop access-challenge stop    -> SURVIVED
```

The tests now supply a healthy route and assert the reason code, which is what makes the refusal attributable to the policy rather than to an empty pool. A third test proves the same request *without* the prohibited input is routable, so the two above cannot pass against a function that refuses everything.

### Routing receipts — a fallback that could leave no trace of which provider ran

Both identity fields in a routing selection could be replaced with `null` with every routing suite green. That is the single failure mode CLAUDE.md's automatic model-failover law exists to prevent: *"Preserve the actual provider/model identity in receipts so UberBond knows what really executed."* `ROUTEID-01/02`.

### `scripts/bootstrap-external-capabilities.mjs` — the sharpest one

The only script whose `--apply` mode spawns commands against the real host, and it had **no test of any kind**. The canon sentence naming what it may not do was the whole of its enforcement, so a seventh step configuring a provider key would have been a clean diff.

The step list moves to `src/external-capability-bootstrap-plan.mjs` with one predicate per clause of that sentence — credentials, starting a service, scans, `--system`/private channels, spend, contact — plus refusals for a shell invocation and for an empty plan (a loop-based predicate returns `ok` for a list of nothing, which would turn "the steps were deleted" into "the boundary holds"). The script fails closed on the audit **before its first spawn**. `BOOTPLAN-01..06`.

## The other thirteen

They close on something weaker than a guard: absence, a compound sentence checked clause by clause against the guard list, or a rule with no runtime representation at all. Three new review classes were needed to say which — `GUARDED_UNDER_DIFFERENT_VOCABULARY`, `ARCHITECTURAL_OBLIGATION`, `DEFINITION_NOT_RULE` — and each entry carries its own residual rather than a summary. Two entries note explicitly that absence is not a guard and nothing would notice if the absent thing arrived.

## Reporting

The doctor now prints the matcher's count and the review record's count as two separate lines. They have different denominators — the matcher's number moves whenever a guard is added, while an entry stays read after its rule becomes guarded — and printing them as one number would let the queue look shorter without anyone having read anything.

```
  backed by a mutation-killed guard: 80 directives, 50 of 155 prohibitions, 29 of 48 external-effect
  unguarded external-effect by the matcher: 19
  review record: 22 entries, 0 unread, 4 real holes found and closed
```

Guard-backed directives 69 → 80; guarded prohibitions 40 → 50.

## Verification at `4cd065b0` (merged head, after taking in `906a05c0`)

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `test:deterministic` | 7630 tests, 7576 pass, **0 fail**, 54 skipped |
| `test:mutation-war:full` | **464 mutations, 464 killed, 0 not killed** |
| `check:syntax` | 2160 files parse |
| `test:relay-safety` | pass |
| `test:wallbreaker` / `external-capabilities` / `nullstar` / `sovereign-coverage` | 16 / 20 / 20 / 38, all pass |
| canon freshness | pass |

Every gate was re-run after the merge, not carried over from before it. Each of the thirteen new guards was also confirmed killed individually by the real harness.

`main` moved to `906a05c0` (the outreach canary) while this was open and conflicted two generated files. Both were resolved by regenerating with `npm run readiness` at the merged head rather than by editing either side — a hand-merged readiness artifact describes a tree that never existed.

One process note worth recording: an early full-suite run appeared to kill a wallbreaker mutation, but the failure was `worker-context-admission`, which refuses on a dirty tree — including the tree my own mutation had just dirtied. No registered guard lists that suite, so the existing 451 kills are not inflated by it; it only misled an ad-hoc run.

## Vercel

Both Vercel checks are red, and are red on `main` at `6f3bd9af`, `5b9c52e8` and `a378cf7f` as well. The build command passes locally at this head, nothing in the diff reaches the deployed surface, and `lite/` is untouched. I cannot read the build log to diagnose further — the Vercel credential in this session returns `403 Forbidden` for `prj_RWUPf14w1xIz9NK92AbNW5z7qDCg`. Detail in [the standing-down comment](https://github.com/mohammedwessam2007/uberbondd/pull/916#issuecomment-5707274431). This does not claim the deployment is fine; it claims the failure is not this PR's and not repairable from here.

title: V3 A001/A021: compile the constitution so its rules can be asked about
body:
The canon is prose, and prose cannot be checked. Nine files carry a few hundred normative statements — "never", "must not", "may only" — and nothing in the repository knew which of them any test enforces.

That gap was not theoretical. The reserved-domain guard and the mailbox-address guard recovered in #914 were both constitutional rules (*no unauthorized external effects*, *authority may narrow but never widen*) with nothing enforcing them, and both were found by accident during unrelated branch archaeology rather than by asking.

## What it does

`src/constitution-compiler.mjs` turns the canon into **262 Directive Objects** — 155 prohibitions, 64 obligations, 43 permissions — each with a content-derived id so an edited rule becomes a new one needing re-review, tagged by whether it governs an external effect, and linked to evidence.

`npm run constitution:doctor` runs it and reports coverage.

## The linkage is two tiers, and they are not the same claim

**Vocabulary overlap with a test file** shows a test discusses the same subject. It says nothing about whether that test would fail if the rule were broken.

**A mutation anchor** is different: a protection that was deliberately removed and a test that went red because of it. So the number worth reporting is the second one:

```
262 directives from 9 canon files
permission 43, obligation 64, prohibition 155
backed by a mutation-killed guard: 69 directives,
  40 of 155 prohibitions, 26 of 48 external-effect
```

## The other 22 are a queue, not a defect count

The doctor cannot yet tell a genuine hole from a compound sentence whose pieces are enforced separately, a keyword false positive, or a rule enforced by absence. Reading five of them found one of each and **no hole**:

- *"Do not infer private contact information, bypass CAPTCHA…"* — one sentence, four prohibitions, enforced across `robots.mjs`, `browser-crawler.mjs`, `capability-genome-admission.mjs` and others. No single guard matches because no single code path does.
- *"Do not invent observations to satisfy a quota"* — tagged on "quota", which here means a Task Observer count, not a provider limit.
- *"Do not infer private contact information"* specifically — **enforced by absence**. `contacts.mjs` sources addresses only from crawled page text filtered to the company domain and from the Hunter provider; nothing constructs an address from a name pattern, so there is no inference path to guard. `lead-generation.mjs:554` carries the explicit stop rule.

Those readings are recorded in `artifacts/constitution/reviewed-linkage-findings.json` with their reasons. An entry closes by being read, never by tuning the matcher until the count falls.

## Evidence

- 7617 tests, 7563 pass, 0 fail, 54 skipped
- 451/451 mutations killed, including 4 new anchors — one reorders the classifier so "must never" reads as an obligation, one removes the code-fence filter so a hierarchy diagram becomes a rule
- 17 compiler tests
- `check:syntax` 2157 files parse; reachability and coverage ratchets green

Also corrects `docs/NULLSTAR_TERMINAL_SUMMARY.md`: the ledger reads `SOFTWARE_SIDE_COMPLETE` again, and it now says plainly that this covers CD001–CD013 and is **not** a completion claim for the V3 program, whose constitution compiler is the only part that exists yet.

Zero external effects. No provider call, spend, deployment, credential or customer mutation.

title: EVENT HORIZON: close CD011 and CD012 by archaeology, recovering two outbound guards
body:
Closes the last two open software items in the completion-debt ledger. Both were "read the thing rather than sample it" work, and both turned up a real safety gap on an outbound path.

## CD012 — 101 stranded pre-rewrite modules, 3 of them checked

`scripts/nullstar-stranded-supersession.mjs` places each module against main by export identity first, distinctive filename token second, and `ABSENT` when neither. 89 placed automatically. 12 came back ABSENT — which is the point, since a checker that cannot return ABSENT is a rubber stamp — and those were read individually into `stranded-absent-determinations.json` with the successor named per module, including two entries that say plainly that main's successor is narrower than what was stranded.

Eleven were superseded. One was a real gap.

**`src/reserved-domains.mjs` was genuinely absent.** Nothing anywhere in main guarded RFC 2606 domains, and `registerSendingDomain` accepted `example.test` as an `OWNER_CONFIRMED` outreach sending domain — reachable from `job-handlers.mjs:483` and `uberdoso-job-handler.mjs:31`, so a fixture domain could become a real send target. Ported and wired at that boundary, failing closed unless the caller declares `simulation: true` literally, because a truthy value is how a fixture becomes real by accident. The event records `simulationOnly` so a declared fixture stays identifiable in the log.

A test written against the RFC rather than against the code caught a defect in the recovered original: it matched only the bare second-level name, so `mail.example.org` passed straight through. Subdomains are reserved now too.

## CD011 — three diverged branches with no terminal disposition

Decided on content, not on ancestry (§0076) and not by relabelling (§0077).

**`feat/outreach-100k-certified-launch-20260915` → SUPERSEDED.** Main carries an evolved superset: the branch derives a child per-recipient authorization from a parent founder press, and main validates the same binding at corpus certification, pins the corpus by `recipientSetDigest`, re-checks that digest in both bundle and job payload, and adds suppression preclearance, legal evidence, business window, mailbox cadence and per-mailbox caps the branch never had.

One check was on the branch and nowhere in main: **`mailbox-authenticated-address-required`**. Main read `address` only as a fallback for `domainId`, so an explicitly supplied `domainId` won and a mailbox could certify against a DNS-verified, warmed, authenticated domain while its real sending address belonged to a different one — a From-domain nothing had ever verified, certified to send a hundred thousand messages. Ported with three tests, including the substring case where `endsWith` alone would accept `evil-uberbond.agency`.

**Both big-button branches → SUPERSEDED.** The capability is in main as `brokerOutreach100kStart`, reached only by an authenticated HTTP request — the founder-interactive entry FD001's `ifNo` branch named. What was rejected was the operator-script entry, not the button, and those scripts stay out. FD001 is recorded as no longer gating a branch; the policy question is not answered and no outbound module was reclassified to close it.

Their residual is named rather than dropped: main's press has no expiring nonce bound to the packet digest. Adding one changes the endpoint's contract for its callers, so it is a follow-up rather than something to take unilaterally.

## Both guards only ever narrow

Neither can permit a send that was previously refused. Nine fixtures now declare themselves — seven as simulations, two by carrying the address they always should have had — rather than the guards being loosened to accommodate them.

title: Stop ancestry from laundering a reverted branch into convergence
body:
## The defect

The branch-debt measurement merged in #912 classified any ancestor of main as `CONTAINED_IN_MAIN`.

Merging a branch and then reverting it leaves its tip an ancestor of main while none of its content is there. So the two big-button branches — the ones held back over the outbound-authority boundary in #912 — went from `DIVERGED` to `CONTAINED_IN_MAIN` the moment they were reverted, and dropped out of the debt count entirely.

An instrument built an hour earlier, producing a false zero in the one case it most needed to be right about. It is the same failure as the disposition check that accepted any label rather than a terminal class, one layer down: the count closed on the shape of the history instead of the state of the tree.

## The fix

Containment is verified against content. A branch counts as contained only if its own `src`, `scripts`, `tests` and `api` files are present in main; otherwise it is `MERGED_THEN_REVERTED`, stays in the list the completion ledger reads, and names the absent files.

```
feat/command-center-big-button    3 files absent  (api/uberlaunch.mjs, src/uberlaunch-runtime.mjs, ...)
feat/founder-big-button-outreach  4 files absent  (src/sovereign-outreach-big-button.mjs, ...)
```

The first attempt at this check did not fire either. It used a three-dot diff, and for a branch that is already an ancestor that resolves the merge-base to the branch itself and returns nothing — so it silently passed everything it was written to catch. It reads the branch's own tree now.

## Populations after the fix

854 remote branches: 735 pre-rewrite lineage, 94 contained, 23 diverged, 2 merged-then-reverted.

## Verification at `00107b3e`

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| Deterministic suite | 7588 tests, 7534 pass, 0 fail, 54 skipped |
| Canon freshness | green at this head |
| New tests | 6, covering the revert case from both sides |

The regression test asserts both halves — that a branch recorded as reverted really is an ancestor of main, and that its recorded files really are absent. Either alone is the condition that fooled the first version.

## Unchanged

`softwareOpen` stays 2. FD001 is still open: whether an outbound send path may be reachable from an unattended operator script. Revenue, customers and cleared payment remain zero. `ASI_STATUS`, `INTELLIGENCE_EXPLOSION_STATUS` and `SINGULARITY_STATUS` remain `NOT_ESTABLISHED`.

title: EVENT HORIZON: branch-debt convergence, UBER/OS integration, and one authority question
body:
## What this is

EVENT HORIZON phases 1 to 4. Branch debt measured, seven stranded branches integrated, two reverted on an authority boundary, and one decision left for you.

- Base main at start: `755e00a2`
- Branch head: `48795773`
- Zero behind main.

## Branch debt, measured

854 remote branches. The raw figure of "767 with unique commits" is almost entirely an artifact: main was rebuilt on a new root, so 735 branches share no ancestor with it and counting their unreachable commits gives numbers above 1700 for a single branch.

| population | count |
|---|---|
| contained in main | 88 |
| genuinely diverged | 31 |
| pre-rewrite lineage | 735 |

Ancestry cannot say whether anything is stranded, so it was measured at file level: 152 pre-rewrite branches carry a file main lacks, 367 distinct files, 101 of them src modules, and **none of those 101 was ever in main's history**. They were not deleted; they never crossed the rewrite.

Three that map to named constitution organs were checked against main. `causal-intervention-ladder` is superseded by `epistemic-immune-system`'s `causalClaim` over Pearl rungs. `decision-information-theory` by `forecast-stack`, which exports `valueOfInformation` and `predictionHalfLife` under the same names. `attribution-chain` by `causal-attribution-spine`, inferred from domain rather than matching exports.

Three of a hundred and one is a pattern, not a proof. The residual is carried as open debt.

## All 31 diverged branches classified

10 superseded, 9 archived donors, 9 merged, 3 without a terminal class.

Seven integrated, each new module gated on what would actually release it rather than a shared label:

- **UBER/OS Generation-0** — buildroot external tree, kernel adapter, system compiler, package provenance, state engine, QEMU scripts. 21 files. `NO_BUILT_UBEROS_IMAGE`: the manifest's kernel revision is still the literal placeholder `CAPTURE_EXACT_VERSION_IN_BUILD_RECEIPT`, so no image exists and no machine runs it.
- **free runtime mesh** — `NO_PROVISIONED_FREE_RUNTIME_MESH`. It already refuses to treat a dispatch as a business effect; there is no worker to dispatch to.
- **owned-target security verifier** — `NO_AUTHORIZED_SECURITY_TARGET`. Its target classes are `OWNED_LOCAL` and `OWNED_PREVIEW` and neither is registered.
- **commercial execution path materializer** — `NO_CUSTOMER`. It marks its own routes `MATERIALIZED_UNPROVEN` without outcome evidence.
- **public research adapter mesh** — `NO_CONFIGURED_EGRESS_ROUTES`.
- Contabo preflight operator and the event-driven runtime witness, both reachable through their own scripts.

## Main was red before this

Eight tests were failing on `origin/main` with none of this branch's work present, verified in a clean worktree. `UBEROCEAN` had been added to `UBER_SOVEREIGN_LAYERS` and to neither the orchestration dependency graph nor the phase list, so the topology could not resolve at all and six tests failed, plus two reachability failures.

Fixed by wiring UberOcean in rather than by deleting assertions — `fix/uber-sovereign-stack-count` had attempted the latter, which greens one test and leaves the topology broken. The tests now assert registry/graph/phase agreement instead of a literal 28, so the next layer added to one place and not the others fails with its own name.

A rival branch had solved the reachability half independently and better in one respect: its `RESEARCH_ONLY` category is more truthful than the gate I had written, because a research instrument is not waiting on anything external. Took their category, their gate name and their authorization language; kept my per-module reasons, since theirs was one boilerplate string repeated nineteen times.
